provenance: Drafted by the assistant on 2026-11-02 by reading src/tools/tvm.py of the pinned commit line by line. The module's own code was not executed; each bug follows from Python semantics on the lines cited. Not checked by a person: the owner must review every item before the numbers are trusted.

bugs.what: growth_multiple divides by pv, so a present value of 0 raises ZeroDivisionError.
Only growth_rate > 0 takes the growing branch, so a negative growth rate silently falls through to the simple PMT / r result and ignores the growth.
A simple perpetuity divides by r, so an annual rate of 0 raises ZeroDivisionError instead of returning an error like the growing branch does.
Rule of 72 divides by annual_rate, and the exact formula divides by log(1 + rate/100), so a rate of 0 raises ZeroDivisionError.
required_monthly_savings divides by (1+r)^n - 1 (and by n when r is 0); for a period under one month n is 0, so this raises ZeroDivisionError.

requirements.statement: Future value with n compounding periods per year is PV x (1 + r/n)^(n x t).
Compounding periods of 0 mean continuous compounding, FV = PV x e^(r x t).
Future value also reports the simple interest and the compounding benefit over it.
An annuity has int(years x periods per year) payments.
An annuity due is worth the ordinary annuity times (1 + r).
A growing perpetuity needs the required return to exceed the growth rate, otherwise an error is returned.
Rule of 72 also reports the exact years to double, log 2 / log(1 + rate/100).
The real rate of return uses the Fisher equation (1 + nominal) / (1 + inflation) - 1.
If current savings will already exceed the target, the monthly savings needed is 0 with a message.
